judgment.rationale: First PO develops the idea of length (Topic: Length); second compares weights of common objects using light/heavy (Topic: Weight). Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under the same Sub-Theme 'Primary Measures' within MENSURATION AND GEOMETRY, addressing introductory measurement of physical attributes through direct comparison. This is substantive conceptual coherence between complementary measurement skills, but proficiency in one does not specifically enable the other (distinct attributes/topics, same rank), so no directional buildsTowards is justified. Shared ancestry and weak token/page/rank proximity alone are only reasons to examine, not to assert dependency.

judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same PRIMARY TWO Topic '1. Three dimensional shapes' (Sub-Theme Shapes, Theme Mensuration and Geometry). The first asks pupils to mention real-world cylinder and sphere objects in the home; the second asks pupils to identify and count edges of a cube and cuboid. These are complementary skills exploring different attributes of 3D shapes (real-world recognition vs. structural features like edges), giving substantive conceptual coherence within the same 3D-shapes topic. However, they target different shapes and different skills with no clear developmental dependency, and both sit at the same grade rank (rank 1, PRIMARY TWO), so no lower-to-higher direction is supported. Proficiency in one is not a clear precondition for success in the other, so relatesTo is preferred over buildsTowards. Shared token overlap is dominated by generic stem words ('pupils should be able to') and is not itself semantic evidence.

judgment.rationale: First SFI is a Primary Three Performance Objective to multiply whole numbers from 1 x 1 to 9 x 9 (Topic: 3. Multiplication); second is a Primary Three objective to express whole numbers not exceeding 48 as products of factors (Topic: 4. Division). Both sit under the same Basic Operations Theme/Sub-Theme at rank 2. Expressing a number as products of factors depends on command of multiplication facts (times tables), so proficiency in the multiplication objective substantively supports success in the factorization objective, justifying a same-rank directional buildsTowards first_to_second beyond mere shared hierarchy or token overlap.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Three dimensional shapes' (Sub-Theme Shapes, Theme Mensuration and Geometry). One asks pupils to distinguish between cuboids and cubes; the other to mention solid shapes found in homes and the environment. They share substantive conceptual coherence around recognizing and describing 3D/solid shapes, with LC tags overlapping on '3d shapes'. However, neither objective is a clear prerequisite for the other: identifying/naming shapes in the environment and comparing cuboids versus cubes are complementary facets of the same topic rather than a developmental dependency, and both sit at the same PRIMARY ONE rank with no evidence establishing direction. relatesTo is the best-supported permitted decision.

judgment.rationale: Both are Primary One Performance Objectives under the same Topic '1. Three dimensional shapes' (Sub-Theme Shapes, Theme Mensuration and Geometry). The first objective is sorting cubes, cuboids, cylinders and spheres; the second is mentioning solid shapes found in homes and the environment. They share substantive conceptual coherence about 3D/solid shapes and reinforce one another. Both sit at the same Grade rank (PRIMARY ONE, rank 0), and there is no clear directional dependency evidence—recognizing solid shapes in the environment does not strictly require prior sorting proficiency, and vice versa—so a symmetric relatesTo best fits rather than a developmental direction. LC tag overlap ('3d shapes') supports the conceptual link, while the token/trigram/page-proximity signals are boilerplate ('pupils should be able to') and not semantic.

judgment.rationale: Both are Performance Objectives under the same PRIMARY TWO / MENSURATION AND GEOMETRY / Shapes / Three Dimensional shapes topic. One asks pupils to identify the curved surfaces of a cylinder; the other to identify and count the edges of a cube and cuboid. These are complementary component-identification skills for 3D solids—substantive conceptual coherence within one topic—but neither establishes a dependency on the other, and both sit at the same Grade rank (PRIMARY TWO, rank 1) with no evidence that proficiency in one supports success in the other. Shared tokens are generic stem wording ('pupils should be able to', 'identify', 'the', 'a'), not developmental evidence, so relatesTo is the supported judgment rather than buildsTowards.
